stories.primary_headline: Germany says Russia behind Leipzig airport drone attack

primary_source.headline: Germany says Russia behind Leipzig airport drone attack
primary_source.content: A drone carrying an explosive device was discovered at Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany, close to Ukrainian cargo planes, on 4 August. It failed to explode as the detonator was apparently faulty, and investigators suspect a second drone collided with a cargo aircraft nearby. A third drone was reportedly found near the airport 10 days later. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the Leipzig airport attack followed the "well-established pattern of Russian hybrid operations in Europe" and the assumption was that Germany would be targeted again. Security experts had speculated that Russia may have been responsible, however Russia has always rejected claims of involvement. Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany is used by the Germany military and Nato allies for the transport of military goods and also serves as a base for Ukraine's Antonov Airlines - which carries most of the country's aerial cargo. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul, who was standing beside Dobrindt at a press conference in Berlin, said he would order the closure of the Russian consulate in Bonn, and the contract for the Russian House in Berlin will also be terminated - which many observers have said has been used for espionage and to spread Russian propaganda.

primary_source.headline: Death toll from Russian strike on Ukrainian arms depot rises to 38 - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: The death toll from a Russian strike on an arms depot near the Ukrainian capital, Kyiv, has risen to 38, marking the war’s deadliest attack so far this year, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said. Emergency workers on Sunday continued to extinguish the resulting fires and explosions that began on Saturday in the village of Myla, Zelenskyy said in a post on Telegram, adding that bomb disposal teams were also working to clear the site. He said 20 people were injured, while four remained missing. The attack was the second to hit a munitions depot near Kyiv within two months, with officials voicing anger that arms were still being stored so close to residential areas. Separately, Zelenskyy said in a video message that Kyiv is preparing for a new round of talks with representatives of US President Donald Trump, with further details expected on Monday. Zelenskyy stressed that Ukraine is “doing everything possible to ensure that war does not remain the only option for future developments”, even as Moscow intensifies its strategy of exhaustion.

primary_source.headline: Pakistan: 21 terrorists killed in clashes with security forces in Balochistan
primary_source.content: Islamabad: At least 21 terrorists have been killed in two separate clashes between security forces and rebels in Pakistan's restive Balochistan province, the Pakistan army said on Tuesday.The incidents took place on Monday night in Nokcha, Chagai district and Ziarat Cross, Pishin district, during which five security personnel and one Customs official were also killed, the army said in a statement.It said that twenty-one terrorists belonging to Fitna al-Khawarij were eliminated following effective responses by the security forces.Security forces kill 11 terrorists in various operations in Pakistan's Balochistan, KPKFitna al-Khawarij is a term that the state uses for the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).In the first incident, the terrorists attempted to disrupt the movement of commuters along N-40 Quetta–Taftan Highway by establishing an illegal checkpoint for extortion.&nbsp; “Security Forces responded immediately and, after an intense fire exchange, killed eleven terrorists on the spot,” it said.A large quantity of weapons, ammunition and explosives was also recovered from the terrorists.In the second incident, terrorists launched a coordinated attack in an attempt to breach the Customs House.&nbsp; “Security Forces responded effectively and, after an intense fire exchange, killed ten terrorists,” the army said.The attack on the Customs House was carried out to prevent Customs officials from performing their lawful duties, it added.The army said that five security personnel and a Customs official were also killed during the exchange of fire.Sanitisation operations are being conducted in the surrounding areas to eliminate any remaining terrorists and ensure the safety and security of the local population as well as the vital national highways.Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terror activities, particularly in its Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan provinces in the past few years.The monthly report of the Islamabad-based think tank, the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS), said on July 31 that the security situation deteriorated most significantly in Balochistan last month.The overall death toll increased by 241 per cent in Balochistan, from 109 in June to 372 in July, the PICSS said.It also said that 62 security personnel were killed in different incidents and operations in Balochistan in July, compared to six killed in June.Security forces, including the military, have been carrying out clean-up operations in Balochistan after a spate of attacks by insurgent groups, especially one incident which saw 27 policemen killed in Ziarat on July 6.

stories.primary_headline: India rejects Hague court order to restore Indus waters pact with Pakistan

primary_source.headline: India rejects Hague court order to restore Indus waters pact with Pakistan - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: India has rejected a ruling by the Permanent Court of Arbitration in The Hague ordering it to uphold the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty with Pakistan, saying the tribunal has no jurisdiction over the matter. India suspended the treaty in April last year after identifying two of three assailants as Pakistani in an attack that killed 26 people at a Kashmir tourist destination. Pakistan denied any involvement in the attack. The standoff places the decades-long conflict over Kashmir as the primary trigger behind the collapse of the historic water pact, pushing a framework that had endured three wars past its breaking point. Under the 1960 agreement, these shared river systems feed 80 percent of Pakistan’s agricultural land. India’s rejection follows the international court’s ruling on Monday that the pact remains fully binding and that India had no justification for ending or suspending it. The tribunal ordered India to limit construction on the Ratle Hydro-Electric Plant in Kashmir, prohibiting work on the dam wall and power intake structure above certain levels. These restrictions will remain in place until 90 days after a World Bank-appointed neutral expert delivers a decision, expected by July 2027. The Indian Ministry of External Affairs, however, said the country does not recognise the court and “categorically” rejected the verdict.

stories.primary_headline: Rescuers search for missing workers as Nepal-China death toll nears 800

primary_source.headline: Rescuers search for missing workers as Nepal-China death toll nears 800 - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Rescuers in Nepal are scrambling to save more than 900 workers believed to be trapped underground at hydropower projects following last week’s devastating floods, the country’s disaster management authority has said. At least 933 workers are understood to be stuck in tunnels at about six hydropower projects, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said on Monday. At least 797 people were killed on the border of Nepal and the Chinese territory of Tibet after part of a glacier collapsed in the Himalayas on Wednesday at an altitude of roughly 5,200 metres (17,000 feet) and plunged approximately 1,200 metres (3,900 ft), gathering rock and debris before slamming into the Lhende River in Tibet. The descent and plunge sent water and debris surging downstream into Nepal, creating a lake across the border that overflowed through the Trishuli and Bhote Koshi river corridors, destroying several villages. About 3,048 people remain missing. Nepal said on Sunday that at least 781 had been killed on its side of the border, with 2,502 people missing, including 592 foreign nationals. In China, state broadcaster CCTV reported 16 deaths and 546 people missing, including 261 foreigners.

primary_source.headline: Trump says US position on Falklands 'one of many' under review
primary_source.content: The US president said the UK has "got some problems, but they'll get solved" when asked about defence funding as a follow-up question to his response on the Falklands. The UK government responded by saying Falkland islanders "are British with a right to determine their own future". A spokesperson added: "The islanders have repeatedly expressed their wish to remain a British overseas territory and our commitment to them is unwavering." The Falkland Islands, in the south-west Atlantic Ocean, remain the subject of a sovereignty dispute between Britain and Argentina. The two countries waged a brief but bitter war over the territory in 1982. A British military task force ejected Argentine forces, which had landed on the Falklands to stake a territorial claim. The 74-day conflict led to the deaths of 255 British military personnel, three islanders and 649 Argentine soldiers.

stories.primary_headline: Firecracker factory blast in India kills 8 children

primary_source.headline: Firecracker factory blast in India kills 8 children - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Eleven people have been killed as a firecracker factory in India exploded, leaving many injured and destroying several houses. Three adults and eight children were killed in the accident on Monday. Marking yet another fatal blast at an Indian firecracker factory this year. The youngest child killed was just four years old, according to local police. Several injured people were taken to hospital for treatment. Videos circulated on social media with images of the scene in the aftermath of the explosion in northern India’s Uttar Pradesh state. The footage showed nearby houses completely demolished at the site of the explosion. Other images showed survivors covered in debris and dust. Rescue teams used excavators and citizens employed other tools including stones as they searched for survivors under the rubble. The cause for the explosion was not immediately clear. Local authorities were directed to the scene “to ensure proper treatment for the injured and to reach out to the affected families to provide them every possible assistance”, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said on social media.

stories.primary_headline: What should we do with Trump's monstrous architectural legacy? | Jan-Werner Müller

primary_source.headline: What should we do with Trump’s monstrous architectural legacy? | Jan-Werner Müller
primary_source.content: Questions over Trump’s ballroom and other structures might not feel urgent. But when his reign ends, Trumpism must be repudiatedOn Monday, a majority on the supreme court found a technical way to overrule a lower court’s imperative to stop work, while not taking a stance on whether the whole enterprise might be illegal to begin with. Preservationists, the majority held, appear to lack legal grounds for filing a suit blocking Trump’s ballroom; that means construction will proceed, even if none other than John Roberts, in a dissent, held that “those responsible” were breaking the rules in deciding “what to build up at the People’s House”. The solicitor general, John Sauer, is on record claiming that 65% of the project is completed (of course, he might have exaggerated – such things are known to have happened in Trump administrations). Either way, it is thus likely that there will be a massive structure next to the original White House; and, given that the ruling will embolden the president dramatically to change Washington DC’s landscape by spending money never approved by Congress, we might be cursed with a triumphal arch as well. All of which raises the question: what to do with a monstrous architectural legacy in post-Trump America?Some might dismiss the question as a bit of a luxury problem. After all, a war that also demonstrates the ongoing disempowerment of Congress keeps dragging on; ICE continues its cruel day-to-day work; Trump is trying every tactic to make the midterms go his way. But the built environment, and especially the civic landscape of a capital, is never just an afterthought. Buildings and monuments make values visible, as the philosopher Susan Neiman once put it. And the decision to leave Trump’s structures in place as if his reign had just been another normal era in US history is not neutral – just like leaving Confederate monuments in place is not neutral.Jan-Werner Müller is a Guardian US columnist and a professor of politics at Princeton University Continue reading...

primary_source.headline: Trump vows to hit Iran hard, says US escorting dozens of ships in Hormuz - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: United States President Donald Trump has threatened to hit Iran hard and claimed Washington was helping some 30 ships pass through the Strait of Hormuz every night. Trump’s comments on Monday came after the US bombed Iran’s Larak Island and Tehran launched retaliatory strikes targeting US military bases and assets in Jordan and the United Arab Emirates, marking the first exchange of fire in more than a month. Speaking to reporters at the Oval Office, Trump claimed the Strait of Hormuz, which Tehran has blockaded since the start of the US-Israel war in February, was in “extremely good shape”. “We’re taking over. Many, many ships got through last night. As you know, with the navy’s assistance, and we’ve been averaging 30 ships a night,” he said. Earlier, he had promised to respond to Iran’s retaliatory strikes. “We’re going to hit them hard,” he told Fox News. “There will be a response.”

stories.primary_headline: Over 6,000 Ebola cases confirmed in DRC as death toll nears 3,000

primary_source.headline: Over 6,000 Ebola cases confirmed in DRC as death toll nears 3,000 - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has topped prior surges – becoming the worst the country has experienced – as new data confirms there are now over 6,000 confirmed cases and nearly 3,000 deaths. There is currently no approved vaccine or treatment for the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, which is rapidly spreading across the country. The current Ebola outbreak is “the fastest-spreading Ebola epidemic ever recorded”, according to United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, as people continue to be infected with the virus faster than frontline workers can track and respond to new cases. This is partly due to many new infections occurring among people who are not being monitored through contract tracing, according to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention. The DRC Ministry of Communications said on social media that 6,041 cases have been confirmed, “including 1,366 recoveries and 2,911 deaths. [Another] 619 patients are in isolation or hospitalised.” The response to the outbreak faces several challenges as cases are mostly concentrated in the eastern provinces of the DRC where densely-populated areas experience insecurity related to armed conflict, displacement and pre-existing humanitarian challenges. The medical charity Doctors Without Borders says existing health needs, as well as airport closures and flight restrictions, are complicating the provision of healthcare, disrupting the flow of staff, diagnostics, referrals and supply chains.

primary_source.headline: Spain’s Sanchez says Russia, Israel spread disinformation on Ceuta crisis - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has accused Israel and Russia of spreading and amplifying disinformation related to the mass influx of migrants to Ceuta last month, citing research by the European External Action Service (EEAS), the European Union’s foreign service. “After July 30 and 31, rumours and disinformation spread on social networks linked to Russia and Israel, and to an ultra-right international that always uses migration to attack both Spain and Europe and divide it,” Sanchez told Spain’s Cadena Ser radio on Monday. Sanchez said it ⁠was “evident” that the ⁠two countries had used the crisis to criticise ⁠the Spanish government, as ⁠they were at ⁠odds with Madrid over its position on the wars ‌in Ukraine and the Middle East. At least 70,000 people crossed into Spain’s North African enclave from Morocco over several days in late July, triggering a Europe-wide migrant alert. The prime minister also ruled out any responsibility on the part of the Moroccan authorities in the sudden influx of migrants. “No intelligence service with which the Spanish government normally cooperates” had suggested “any … involvement in one way or another of the Moroccan authorities”, Sanchez said.

primary_source.headline: Top officials from Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan to meet in Istanbul - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Turkish officials said on Sunday that the meeting will be attended by foreign ministers, defence ministers, and chiefs of staff from the three nations. According to AFP, the Istanbul meeting will formally establish a “political and defence strategic committee” comprised of such national representatives. Turkish Foreign Ministry sources, quoted by Reuters news agency, said the agenda will cover international security issues, as well as discussions on improving military cooperation and capabilities. The Mecca agreement forms a collective security pact similar to NATO, under which an attack on one member could be considered an attack on all. The alliance was established following the United States-Israel war on Iran. Bangladesh has also stated it is actively considering joining the agreement. The potential expansion is being closely monitored by India, whose Foreign Ministry spokesperson, Randhir Jaiswal, told reporters that New Delhi would take all necessary steps to safeguard its national security.

stories.primary_headline: Nepal-China flood disaster: what's the latest toll, how many are missing?

primary_source.headline: Nepal-China flood disaster: What’s the latest toll, how many are missing? - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: The death toll from devastating floods near the border between Nepal and China has risen to more than 900, with thousands missing following Wednesday’s disaster. Rescue efforts are under way to locate more than 900 missing workers at hydropower projects in central Nepal. Authorities from Nepal and the Tibet region of China have put the total number of missing at just over 3,000, with some bodies washing up in neighbouring India. A glacier collapse high in the Himalaya mountains in Nepal near the border with Tibet triggered Wednesday’s catastrophic flooding and landslides, which buried villages and towns along the Trishuli and Bhotekoshi river systems. On Friday, rising water levels in a new lake formed by the build-up of debris prompted a temporary halt to search efforts amid fears of a second flood. Rescue operations resumed after the lake threat was deemed manageable. Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu, reporting from Beijing, said that Chinese authorities say the risk seems to have been reduced, but it has not disappeared.

stories.primary_headline: Air raids, conscripts and China: How Myanmar's military is regaining ground

primary_source.headline: Air raids, conscripts and China: How Myanmar’s military is regaining ground - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: The rebel fighters who abandoned Falam in Myanmar in April said they gave up the border town near India only after running out of bullets. The fighters had endured a six-month assault by Myanmar’s military, including hundreds of air strikes and a ground campaign by roughly 1,000 troops. The fall of the town, which had been under opposition control for a year, marked a strategic victory for the military: Falam is home to the only airport in Chin State and commands a trade route to the Indian border. Within weeks, three more towns in Chin had fallen, and by late May, the military was claiming control of the entire northern part of the state. “Falam taught us an important lesson,” said Salai William Chin, a member of the rebel Chin Brotherhood. “Capturing a town and holding it are two very different challenges,” he told Al Jazeera. “Holding it for a long period required manpower, logistics, administration, civilian protection and the ability to withstand repeated attacks, especially from the air.” The retreat is part of a broader reversal across Myanmar. The country’s opposition – a loose coalition of militias and ethnic armed organisations fighting the military that seized power in a 2021 coup – has been weakened. Their gains in 2023 and 2024, when coordinated offensives stripped the military of dozens of towns, have given way to a steady withdrawal from the urban centres they had captured.

stories.primary_headline: Relative of Afghans who aided US military deported to Africa

primary_source.headline: Relative of Afghans who aided US military deported to Africa - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: The administration of United States President Donald Trump has deported dozens of people to the Central African Republic, including an Afghan whose family members collaborated with the US military, his lawyer and advocacy groups said. The Afghan man, who is in his early 20s, was granted protection against deportation to Afghanistan by a US judge due to fears of persecution by the Taliban, his lawyer, Alma David, said. Advocacy organisations AfghanEvac, a US-based group that assists Afghan allies, the American Civil Liberties Union, and Human Rights First also confirmed his deportation. His family in Afghanistan had received threats from the Taliban, which governs the country, because of his brothers’ involvement in supporting the US military, according to court documents seen by The Associated Press news agency. One of the Afghan man’s brothers lives in the US and served in the Afghan National Army, which collaborated with the US military before the Taliban seized power in 2021, David said. Another brother was a pilot trained by the US and later killed by the Taliban, she added.

primary_source.content: Hyderabad: Telangana government employees staged a large protest at the state secretariat on Tuesday, marking the first visible sign of discontent among government staff, which is notable given that the bulk of the state's expenditure is directed toward welfare schemes.Organized by the Telangana Secretariat Association, the protest saw employees demand the immediate constitution of the second Pay Revision Commission (PRC), prompt disbursal of six pending installments of Dearness Allowance (DA), and the withdrawal of the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS) in favor of a return to the Old Pension Scheme (OPS). Telangana police arrest bike mechanic from Bihar for rape, murder of 21-year-old nurseThey also called for the swift clearance of pending bills across various departments. The protest comes against the backdrop of a widening fiscal gap that Telangana needs around Rs 22,500 crore every month to meet its financial obligations but is currently able to generate only about Rs 18,500 crore.Last year, Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy referenced this shortfall while addressing government employees, saying that even if pressed, his government could not raise more than Rs 18,500 crore a month. He questioned whether the state should therefore halt its welfare schemes, and cautioned that protests and hunger strikes at this juncture could risk a complete breakdown of government machinery.

stories.primary_headline: 'Classic case of diseased versus guilty mind': Tihar jail psychiatrist on Lindsay Clancy row

primary_source.headline: ‘Classic case of diseased versus guilty mind’: Tihar jail psychiatrist on Lindsay Clancy row
primary_source.content:
A US court of justice is currently deciding the fate of a woman who had killed her three children in an alleged fit of postpartum psychosis, a severe mental illness that can take one away from reality.The jury is currently deliberating on the horrific killings that happened on the evening of January 24, 2023, in a Massachusetts house, with both the defendant and the prosecution having offered their closing statements last week.While the accused has not denied killing her children, she has pleaded ‘not guilty’ by reason of insanity.The case has divided the Americans, some say it was a calculated murder, others call it a terrible tale of neglected postpartum medical needs.It is one of the incidences where the boundary between a guilty and diseased mind gets blurred. To understand how a justice system navigates truth in such complex cases, DH spoke to Dr Vivek Rustagi, a senior psychiatrist at Tihar jail.The psychiatrist has also been associated with cases of national importance like ‘Delhi Rape Case’ (2012) and ‘Butcher of Delhi’.Lindsay Clancy’s case brings neglected 'postpartum psychosis' back into spotlight
The unique case of Lindsay ClancyLindsay Clancy, a 36-year-old woman from Massachusetts was charged with murder of her three children: Cora (5), Dawson (3) and Callan (8 months) in 2023 and since then the accused has been in custody.A trained labor and delivery nurse, Lindsay was living with her children and husband, Patrick Clancy, who is an IT professional and worked mostly from a fully ‘finished’ basement in the house.The family was apparently having a normal life until the middle of September 2022 when Lindsay started to see her mental health getting worse every passing day.Reportedly, she had no recorded history of mental illness, but her second childbirth had some reported physical complications.The accused reportedly went from one doctor to another, changed medicines frequently, had poor sleep and an unsettled anxiety.As per reports, she also briefly got herself into a psychiatric ward in January 2023, in the same time when she had disclosed to her kin that she had ‘scary thoughts’ or a suicidal ideation.&nbsp;However, there is no official documentation for the same other than anecdotal evidence from the family members.On January 24 (2023), she killed her children in the basement using exercise bands and later threw herself out of a second storey window that opened in her bedroom.The act was committed when her husband was shortly away from home to receive a food parcel ordered by Lindsay.&nbsp;While the children couldn’t be rescued in time, Lindsay has become paralyzed from down the waistline.Defendant versus prosecutionAs the case reached to courtroom trials, Lindsay’s lawyer Kevin Reddington maintained that the accused was so mentally ill that she should not be held criminally responsible for the act.To rest his case, he argued that the accused was overmedicated.The defendant also said that the accused had ‘command hallucinations’ or a ‘male voice’ instructing her to kill the kids first so she could kill herself next.However, the prosecution presented it as a case of planned homicide with a motive to get rid of the kids who apparently were a burden to her fragile mental health.Sick mind versus criminal responsibilityWhile mental health disorders may cause people to act in unacceptable ways, it is also common for some with a criminal intent to hide their ill motives behind an unstable mind. Experts have called it ‘malingering’ or fabrication of symptoms for non-medical benefits like escaping legal punishment.DH spoke to Dr Vivek Rustagi to understand postpartum mood disorders, how rationality can coexist in an ill mind, and what justice looks like in such cases.Reporter: What are postpartum mood disorders and how often do women get them?Psychiatrist: To start with, not all women will have postpartum mood disorders. It is not a clinical certainty.&nbsp;For others, the clash of a hormonal surge with changing brain chemistry during childbirth can cause abrupt mood changes.In most frequent cases (nearly 50 per cent), we see new mothers having ‘baby blues’ or a short period of mood fluctuation or low feelings. However, it may fade away on its own in a few weeks and the emotional stability gets restored.Then we have postpartum depression, a relatively severe form of mood disorder. It isn’t as common as baby blues. The woman can have a longer stretch of low mood which can extend up to some months, she can feel fatigued or mentally detached from the child. This often needs to be ruled out by an attending doctor.Postpartum psychosis is a very rare but much dangerous manifestation or complication. It can take her away from reality, she may feel agitated, experience a surge of energy, get restless, won’t sleep much, see or hear things which aren’t there (hallucinations) or start having false beliefs (delusions).&nbsp;At this point, it requires immediate medical intervention as the situation becomes a threat to both the mother and the newborn.Reporter: From the face of it, do you think Lindsay suffered from postpartum psychosis?Psychiatrist: I haven’t evaluated the accused in person, so it would be unfair to make a diagnosis.But, following the trials, I do have some reasons to believe it may not be postpartum psychosis.The very word ‘postpartum’ is the clue. The condition needs to manifest in early weeks of childbirth or it is safe to say at least in the first few months after childbirth. If the symptoms arise four months after nursing the newborn, the element of ‘postpartum’ becomes weak in the clinical context because the hormonal surge caused by pregnancy tends to subside by this time.However, I am not implying that the accused may not have been ill.Some trial representatives have called it generalized anxiety disorder, others have hinted about bipolar disorder. So, exact pinpointing is hard and unfair on my part.I would hesitate to call it a bipolar disorder as no manic episodes have been officially documented in the public record.From the face of it, using my industry knowledge, it looks more like a depression that gradually progressed into psychosis, maybe due to neglected care or maybe due to the alleged irregular intake of drugs.Reporter: Can psychosis occur with both depression and mania?Psychiatrist: Mental health disorders vastly vary in their presentation. Not all conditions take one away from reality but some do and brain chemistry plays a role in it.There are people with unipolar disorders like depression where the mood remains consistently low. Then we have bipolar disorder where there are fluctuating episodes of hyperactivity with low mood.Both depression and bipolar disorder can have psychotic symptoms if left untreated or aggravated.Also, the type of psychosis one experiences will be consistent with the mood disorder in the picture. It could look like hyperactivity, a chaotic state of mind or it could be more mood flattening in nature.For instance, in people with depression, psychosis bends towards the affected having more nihilistic or pessimistic delusions, assuming things like their body is rotting from inside or their kids are becoming very sick.&nbsp;Sometimes, psychosis can show up as grandiose thoughts like thinking one is a messenger of God or things like that. It may look more socially disorganized so to say.In my practice, postpartum psychosis looked more like severe agitation and restlessness in a woman than having an entirely dull expression.This is another reason I think Lindsay less likely had postpartum mood disorder.&nbsp;Reporter: Lindsay reportedly engaged with people normally, seemed unusually calm on the day of killings and took their lives in a logical sequence. Can rationality co-exist with mental illness?Psychiatrist: This is where things get extremely tricky. The entire case rests on this dilemma if the accused planned an efficient homicide or the act was a ritual fanned by her delusions.The defendant has argued that Lindsay had ‘command hallucinations’, although not clinically documented.As per my industry knowledge, command hallucinations are difficult to oppose by the affected. They appear as strong, authoritative voices in one’s mind that are hard to&nbsp; ignore.Many patients having psychosis may have delusions and hallucinations but other functional aspects of their mind may work just fine.It may not be surprising if the accused was able to hold normal conversations, do housekeeping chores in the background of the storm raging inside her head.The unusual calmness can also be true in some cases where the affected has finally submitted to their delusions and the mental conflict has eased down.&nbsp;In fact, this is why some people who commit suicide turn abnormally calm. They have made up their mind and there is no turning back.Reporter: How does a justice body approach such cases?Psychiatrist: Having been a part of such cases, a justice system may primarily look for 'mensrea' or a criminal intent.In Lindsay’s trial, her primary motive to kill her children will be accounted for.If the motive is overlapping with her delusions induced by the illness, such as her killing them thinking her kids would be unsafe on Earth without a mother nursing them or feeling they are more safe when dead, then her intent, though seemingly cruel, is coming from a psychologically twisted place to create greater good.Hence, she may get proven ‘non guilty’ under the provision of insanity.Reporter: How will the United States approach this case? Is there any standard way of testifying insanity in courtrooms?Psychiatrist: The United States does not have a uniform code of testifying insanity in criminal cases.It can vary from state to state and from case to case.In Massachusetts where the ongoing trials are being held, the courts may more commonly use a standard similar to the Model Penal Code which provides insanity defense under some circumstances. However, it cannot be said for certain what code is being used in this particular case.It states that a person is not responsible for criminal conduct if at the time of the act, a mental disease or defect caused them to lack the capacity to ‘appreciate’ the wrongfulness of their conduct or conform their actions to the law of the land.There are many other codes that can testify insanity in the US courts such as the McNaughton rule (a bit more rigid in expression), irresistible impulse, Durham rule (not guilty by reason of insanity) and others.Sometimes, they may apply different codes to come up with a verdict.Reporter: How does the Indian judicial system testify insanity?Psychiatrist: India strictly abides by the McNaughton rules which exempts a person on grounds of insanity if the person did not ‘know’ if their actions were legally wrong. It could be due to a defect of reason or a diseased mind.The provision is codified in Section 84 of the Indian Penal Code (IPS) and carried forward as Section 22 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.Reporter: How does testifying insanity differ between India and the United States?Psychiatrist: The US judiciary bodies take a relatively different approach to assess criminal intent.Unlike McNaughton rules which rely on the extreme polarity of actions (the person must know if their action was either right or wrong)(know or don’t know about its wrongfulness), the Model Penal Code (MPC) makes space for a social and emotional knowing whether an act was right or wrong.Unlike India, the US does not oversimplify intent but accepts it as a layered concept which is governed by many social and emotional factors.&nbsp;In fact, the Model Penal Code (MPC) is a moderate adaptation of McNaughton rules and volitional or irresistible impulse which exempts a person of criminal responsibility if defect of reason or mind has left them in no power to control their impulses or compulsive urges to conform to their conduct to the law.Hence, if you look closely, the US has carefully replaced the word ‘know’ with ‘appreciate’.The Indian judicial system relies more on the absolute knowing or not knowing the wrongfulness of their actions in relation to the law.Reporter: What factors make the case more favorable for Lindsay?Psychiatrist: There are many factors that can go in favor of Lindsay Clancy.To start with, in Massachusetts, the state where the case is being presented, the burden of proving a criminal intent rests on the prosecution and not the defendant.&nbsp;A defendant is presumed to be innocent and is not required to prove their lack of criminal intent or insanity.&nbsp;The entire burden falls on the prosecution which has to convince the jury that there is no other reasonable justification of the act other than the criminal intent of the defendant.In Lindsay’s trial, there is a previous documentation of symptoms and prescriptions, no strong motive to kill children and no prior history of drug abuse.Also, her trying to jump off the window and kill herself can be taken as ‘extended suicide’.All these factors make the legal proceedings more favorable towards her.However, since the verdict is awaited, it would be too soon to jump on any conclusion.Reporter: What can work against her?Psychiatrist: The prosecution has argued that her orchestrating the killings in an allegedly ‘planned’ manner and in absence of the husband shows an active conscience and brings an element of ‘concealment’ to the case.There is a term for it, we call it ‘Deliberate premeditation’ which means the action was planned and not performed in an impulse or an uncontrollable urge.Reporter: As per reports, the accused was asked to discontinue Zoloft 50 mg by her attending psychiatrist Dr Jennifer Tufts when she had reported side effects. Do all psychiatric drugs need to be tapered down? Do you agree that the alleged ‘drug cocktail’ caused her psychosis?Psychiatrist: There are many psychiatric drugs, including the SSRIs (selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor) which are not abruptly stopped but have to be tapered down just like a diabetes medicine or a blood pressure pill.But there are some which can be discontinued, particularly if they are low dosage.Zoloft 50 mg is a relatively low dose prescription and it is common and rather safe for psychiatrists to ask people to discontinue if they are reporting any side effects.All medicines come with side effects which are extremely rare and hardly apply to most of the population.Interestingly, antimalarial medicine can make a person go into psychosis in rarest of cases.Also, psychiatrists don’t blindly offer medicines. We do like to see which one works the best for a specific patient but as an industry, we are particular as to who gets the medicine and even in what counts.If the person has slightest tendency to develop suicidal ideation, we limit the number of doses to prevent them from overdosing it.&nbsp;So, I would not agree with the claim that a ‘cocktail of medicines’ led her to psychosis.Although, if the medicines were not taken as instructed, it could have worsened her condition.Reporter: Is there a blind spot for psychiatry?Psychiatrist: Yes absolutely, just like any other area of medicine we cannot fully determine if our patients are following our instructions or not.Medical non-adherence is way more common than one estimates.Particularly in India, we can see patients randomly stopping diabetes pills or hypertension medicines when they start to feel better.So is the case with psychiatric drugs which carry all the more stigma and apprehensions to it.Reporter: Can postpartum psychosis happen to a person of any race or some lie at greater risk?Psychiatrist: Postpartum psychosis can happen to anyone and anywhere. Some underlying mental health conditions like bipolar disorder, depression and even traumatic birth experience can increase one’s risk.However, it is safe to say that the prognosis of mental health disorders in India is relatively better because of the support fabric and interdependency.&nbsp;Postpartum psychosis in IndiaAs per reports, postpartum psychosis is a severe psychiatric disorder that affects about 1 to 2 about every 1000 mothers in India and worldwide.As per reports, a woman named Aswathi was charged with strangling her one year old daughter in Venjaaramodu (Kerala, 2026), allegedly having a belief that her daughter has autism.Likewise, in 2021, another new mother from Kerala’s Kollam had strangled her toddler and allegedly was suffering from mental health conditions.Need for postpartum careLindsay Clancy’s trial has revealed that though rare, conditions like postpartum psychosis can occur to anyone. It also highlights the need to rethink and upgrade postpartum care of a woman who has just given birth.The case has also highlighted the boundary where a guilty mind ends and criminal responsibility begins.

primary_source.headline: Delhi govt seals Maujpur playschool over toddler's assault, finds multiple building norm violations
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Delhi government has sealed a playschool in northeast Delhi's&nbsp;Maujpur&nbsp;where a three-year-old boy was allegedly physically and sexually assaulted, after an inspection found multiple safety and building norm violations, including blocked emergency exits and a non-functional fire extinguisher.The director of the pre-school and daycare activity centre failed to produce satisfactory replies or the required permissions during the inspection, according to a report prepared by Yamuna Vihar sub-divisional magistrate.3-year-old sexually abused by Delhi school bus driver four times; AAP leader tears into CM Rekha GuptaThe inspection was conducted to check compliance with provisions of the Disaster Management Act, 2005, the Delhi Municipal Corporation Act, 1957, and the Delhi Fire Service Act, 2007, it stated.Bengaluru: How are parents vetting daycares now?According to the report, the playschool did not have a fire safety certificate, a sanctioned building plan, or a completion or occupancy certificate. Its emergency exit and staircases were blocked; the only fire extinguisher at the premises was non-functional.A borewell was found at the playschool premises, for which no permission was produced. The rooms lacked proper ventilation, while the basement had rooms being used to conduct classes in violation of the Delhi Municipal Act, the report said.The school was also found operating in a residential area while carrying out commercial activity and also ran a kitchen on the first floor using domestic LPG cylinders, it said, adding that the sealing was carried out "to ensure public safety".The action comes days after a three-year-old boy was allegedly subjected to hours of physical abuse inside the playschool.In his complaint, the child's father alleged that CCTV footage showed his son being tied to a chair for nearly three hours, beaten and kicked repeatedly.The father also said that in one instance, a person was seen placing hands on the child's private parts. The allegation is part of the complaint and is being investigated by police.The family claimed that the child has since been struggling to pass stool and urine, and has become traumatised.The child's father said he called the police helpline 112 on August 27 from outside the playschool and entered the premises along with police personnel, following which the child was medically examined.The FIR filed accordingly mentioned swelling on the child's left thigh and a superficial abrasion near his left eye. No other external injury was noted during the examination, following which further medical examination was conducted at the GTB Hospital.A case was registered at Jafrabad police station on August 28 against four people: the director, principal, a teacher and a caretaker of the playschool.The FIR invoked Sections 115(2) (voluntarily causing hurt), 126(2) (wrongful restraint) and 3(5) (common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita; provisions of the Juvenile Justice Act; and Section 12 (sexual assault) of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act.A caretaker has been arrested in connection with the case. Another woman has been served a notice to join the investigation, police said.Authorities have seized the CCTV footage and are examining it as part of the investigation, they said.

primary_source.headline: Toxic haze from Indonesian forest fires chokes Malaysian Borneo - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: It is the region’s worst haze episode since 2015, when fires in Indonesia exposed tens of millions of people to toxic smoke and caused more than 500,000 people to suffer respiratory ailments. On Tuesday, six areas in Sarawak recorded hazardous air quality, with readings above 300 on Malaysia’s Air Pollutant Index. Anything above 100 is considered unhealthy. In Kuching, the state capital, the index hit 407, while in Serian, a town close to the Kalimantan border, it hit 408. Mia Emylia Hassan, 33, a mother of two in Kuching, said the smell of smoke was inescapable. “The air here is very thick,” she said. “It smells like smoke, and it’s just white all over.” Visibility from her house, she said, had dropped to about a kilometre, or roughly half a mile. “We have not seen blue sky for over a month,” she said. The haze arrived in early August, shortly after her 10-month-old daughter came home from the hospital after a lung infection. “She’s not healing properly because her lungs are still developing,” Hassan said. “She’s been on medication this whole month, and she has been coughing and vomiting.” Twice, the family has had to rush the infant back to the emergency room because she could not breathe.

primary_source.headline: Palestinian farmers rebuild what Israeli settlers destroy in West Bank - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Along with roughly two dozen other farmers, Najjar is a member of Burin’s Land and Farming Cooperative. They know that they don’t have the capability to fight back against Israel’s military might with arms so instead focus on the land and keeping their connection to it. On July 13, a settler tried to graze his flock inside one of the cooperative’s five greenhouses. Cooperative members struggled to keep the livestock away until Israeli border police arrived. Najjar recalled challenging the officers over why a settler had been permitted onto land the army itself had designated a closed military zone, from which Israeli citizens are, on paper, also barred. The settler left angry. In Arabic, he told Najjar: “You’ll see.” The next night, roughly 10 settlers arrived, gutting all five of the cooperative’s greenhouses, cutting away their plastic sheeting and destroying their irrigation networks. The damage, by the cooperative’s estimate, ran to roughly 30,000 shekels (about $10,000) in plastic sheeting alone. About 9,000 tomato seedlings worth 8,000 shekels ($2,670) had been bought that same morning for planting. They died within hours because there was nowhere else to put them. For a cooperative that pools land, labour and produce among about 25 families, the loss reverberated beyond the five greenhouses themselves. “We’re talking about 25 families working inside the cooperative,” Najjar said. “This year is the most difficult year for the cooperative. We’re facing many attacks by the settlers and the army.”

primary_source.content: Police have detained the captain and seven crew members of a ferry that capsized off Northern Cyprus, killing at least eight of the 270 people on board and leaving 18 others missing. The transport minister of the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Erhan Arikli, told Turkish news agency Anadolu on Sunday that passengers had made several allegations involving the crew, including that the doors had been locked and that the captain fled the vessel. Others said the vessel began taking on water shortly after leaving the port and that crew members had failed to heed their warnings. Arikli said his ministry would launch an investigation separate from the police probe. Al Jazeera correspondent Resul Serdar said that finding those missing at sea was the priority and that “a huge deployment to the area as part of the search and rescue effort affiliated with the Northern Cyprus coastguard command” had begun. primary_source.content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Tuesday came down heavily on Shiv Sena corporator Ramesh Sukrya Mhatre for the alleged assault on doctors at Shastrinagar Hospital in Kalyan, observing that attacks on medical professionals inside hospitals could not be treated lightly and indicating it was inclined to uphold the Bombay High Court’s stay on his bail.A bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Sandeep Mehta and Augustine George Masih was hearing Mhatre’s challenge to the High Court’s July 18 order staying the bail granted to him by a Kalyan magistrate and its August 7 order imposing stringent conditions.&nbsp;Supreme Court quashes FIRs on NEET protesters nationwide, bars fresh casesThe High Court had initiated suo motu proceedings after the magistrate granted bail to Mhatre and his associates.“This is a case where you should have been put in detention. Medical personnel are threatened like this, who will come to the aid of people at large? Absolutely not justified. This kind of people don’t deserve it,” the bench remarked.The court also noted that Mhatre was caught on video and that the footage had gone viral. It emphasised the trauma caused when a mob attacks inside a hospital.Senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi, appearing for Mhatre, argued that the High Court erred in taking suo motu cognisance and staying the bail order without giving him a hearing, including through a special Saturday sitting.&nbsp;He also questioned the High Court’s directions on completing investigation, filing the chargesheet and framing charges within fixed timelines.The Supreme Court rejected these submissions, holding that the High Court was fully justified in intervening.&nbsp;“You are a public elected person,” the bench observed. It indicated it found no fault with the July 18 stay order.Advocate Siddharth Dharmadhikari, representing the State of Maharashtra, informed the court that the state would file a special leave petition the same day challenging the High Court’s August 7 order that had granted bail to Mhatre with conditions.&nbsp;The Indian Medical Association also intervened to oppose bail.The bench directed that the state’s challenge, once filed, be listed along with Mhatre’s petition on Monday.The case arose from a July 6 incident involving a nine-month pregnant woman allegedly kept waiting at the Kalyan-Dombivli Municipal Corporation-run hospital. primary_source.headline: ‘False and objectionable’: UP Cong president Ajay Rai files defamation case against CM Yogi over ‘fish feast’ remarks
primary_source.content: Lucknow: Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai on Tuesday filed a defamation case against chief minister Yogi Adityanath over the latter’s reported remarks regarding organizing a ‘fish feast’ by the former in Ayodhya recently.Rai filed the defamation case in the Civil Court here.In his petition, Rai said that the allegations leveled in this connection by Adityanath were ‘false’ and ‘objectionable’.'An insult to Hindu traditions': UP CM Adityanath hits Congress over fish feast during Shravana‘’An attempt was made to tarnish my public image and reputation by presenting incorrect facts…….leveling wrong and baseless allegations against anyone in public life is a serious matter,’’ he said in his petition.It was alleged that a ‘fish feast’ was organised during Rai’s event in Ayodhya in the ongoing sacred Hindu month of Shravana. Several Ayodhya based seers and Adityanath had termed it as reflective of Congress’ ‘anti-Sanatan’ mindset and sought an apology from the grand old party.‘’Organising a fish feast during Shravana is an insult to Sanatan Dharma as well as Ayodhya and Congress must tender a public apology,’’ Mahant Bharat, an Ayodhya based seer had said.He said that Congress had no ‘respect’ for the Hindu sentiments and ‘Sanatan Dharma’ and that such an insult would never be tolerated by the seers.Adityanath had also, while addressing a public meeting, slammed Congress saying that it was an ‘insult’ to Hindu traditions and religious beliefs. ‘’Congress has always been anti-Sanatan’’, he had remarked.A bone of contention: BJP picks on Congress over fish feast in Ayodhya during 'Sawan' monthRai, however, denied the allegations stating that he had attended a program organised by the ‘Nishad’ (fishermen) community in Ayodhya but no non-vegetarian food was served there. ‘’BJP is insulting the Nishad community by levelling such allegations,’’ he added.He had also challenged the BJP to furnish proof of their allegations.The controversy had erupted after a video, purportedly showing fish being served at the event attended by Rai, went viral on social media platforms.

primary_source.headline: Led by Rahul Gandhi, Maharashtra Opposition mounts vote-chori charge
primary_source.content: Mumbai: With more than 2.06 crore electors excluded from Maharashtra’s draft electoral roll after the SIR exercise, the Maha Vikas Aghadi-INDIA opposition reiterated allegations of vote-chori with Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi spearheading the charge.&nbsp;It may be mentioned that after the 2024 Maharashtra Legislative Assembly elections, in which the BJP-led Maha Yuti swept the polls with a never-seen-before verdict, Gandhi had made allegations of vote theft.&nbsp;“The BJP and the 'Vote Theft Commission' keep changing their tactics, and they will continue to do so—the goal remains just one: BJP's victory at any cost, and the end of India's democracy,” Gandhi said slamming the BJP and the Election Commission.&nbsp;'Only goal is BJP's victory at any cost' | Rahul Gandhi revives ‘vote chori’ campaign“In Maharashtra&nbsp;&nbsp;in 2024, suddenly, 39 lakh new voters were added between the Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha elections. I said it then, and I say it today: This was vote theft.&nbsp;Before the SIR, Maharashtra had 9.78 crore voters, of whom 78.86 per cent made it to the draft roll.”The Maharashtra Pradesh Congress Committee (MPCC) pointed out that the&nbsp;list&nbsp;also includes&nbsp;the&nbsp;names of suspicious&nbsp;and&nbsp;unmapped&nbsp;voters;&nbsp;but no mark has been put on those names. “This will create confusion among the voters, these voters will be called for a hearing by giving a notice,” it said, demanding that&nbsp;a booth-wise list of voters to whom notices are&nbsp;to be issued&nbsp;be published immediately and made available to political parties.Congress has expressed fear that&nbsp;BLOs will use the same method&nbsp;as in Maharashtra where 1.52 crore voters were not found or were shown as permanently displaced&nbsp;,&nbsp;and that crores more voters will be excluded from the voter list.Congress MLA Amin Patel said&nbsp;that in the new list, the names of approximately two crore people have been deleted from Maharashtra, while around 35–40 percent of names have been deleted in Mumbai.“When the SIR process began, we had written to the Election Commission and raised the issue, telling them that the process was not being carried out properly. BLOs were not going to people’s homes, and people were being marked as unavailable,” Patel said, alleging that the SIR process was rigged.&nbsp;NCP national spokesperson and secretary Clyde Crasto said: “Shocking that two crore voters’ names deleted from the draft Maharashtra SIR list. Some of these voters voted for the BJP in the last elections. So does this deletion of names now give any validity to the BJP led government in Maharashtra?”Congress leader in the Legislative Council Satej Patil said that Gandhi has flagged the sudden addition of around 39 lakh voters in just 5 months between 2024 Lok Sabha and&nbsp;Vidhan Sabha polls. “Those were more than the previous 5 years' addition and now comes a sharp drop,” he said, demanding that the EC must provide&nbsp;&nbsp;full comparable machine-readable data of 2024 Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha and pre-SIR rolls.BJP defends processBJP MLA and spokesperson Ram Kadam said that the BLOs have visited the homes. "The SIR process is a transparent process. Anyone can sit at home and get their name registered, and the BLOs are going door to door,” he said and wanted to know what exactly the opposition wants. “There are names appearing four times in the voter list, and there are also names of people who have died. Should those names not be removed? What is the opposition's strategy behind keeping the same names four times?,” he said and alleged that the Congress created a fake narrative ahead of the 2024 Lok Sabha polls that the Constitution is going to be changed.&nbsp;

primary_source.headline: 'Only goal is BJP's victory at any cost' | Rahul Gandhi revives ‘vote chori’ campaign
primary_source.content:
New Delhi: Citing the deletion of 2.07 crore names from Maharashtra draft electoral rolls, top Congress leader Rahul Gandhi revived the ‘vote chori’ campaign on Tuesday claiming that the “goal of the BJP and ‘Vote Chori’ Commission” is to ensure the saffron party's victory.He also recalled his claim of suspicious addition of nearly 40 lakh voters in five months between Lok Sabha and Assembly elections in Maharashtra and said for a government built on 'vote chori', the people are not important and that is why the BJP neither listens to the people nor obeys their command."The BJP and the 'Vote Theft Commission' keep changing their tactics, and they will continue to do so -- the goal remains just one: BJP's victory at any cost, and the end of India's democracy," he said on 'X'.भाजपा और 'वोट चोरी आयोग' के तरीके बदलते रहते हैं, और बदलते रहेंगे - मकसद बस एक ही है: किसी भी क़ीमत पर BJP की जीत, और भारत के लोकतंत्र का अंत।महाराष्ट्र 2024 - लोकसभा और विधानसभा चुनाव के बीच अचानक 39 लाख नए वोटर जुड़ गए। मैंने तब भी कहा था, आज भी कहता हूँ: यह वोट चोरी थी।…&mdash; Rahul Gandhi (@RahulGandhi) September 1, 2026
 

His remarks came as Maharashtra Chief Electoral Office released the draft electoral rolls on Monday following the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in which 2,06,88,487 names were deleted from the voter list, which had 9,78,54,049 names. The draft list has 7,71,65,562 names, which is 78.86% of the pre-SIR voter list."Maharashtra 2024 -- suddenly, 39 lakh new voters were added between the Lok Sabha and Assembly elections. I said it then, and I say it today: This was vote theft. Bengal 2026 -- of the names struck off in the SIR, 91% had to be reinstated after appeals. That means 9 out of every 10 names were wrongly deleted, and added back only after the election. I said it then, and I say it today: This was vote theft," Rahul said.Over 3,400 SIR forms found at private photocopy centre in Maharashtra; 5 BLOs suspended"And now in Maharashtra, 2.07 crore voters have been removed from the draft lis -- that's every fifth voter. Lok Sabha 2024: 9.29 crore. Assembly 2024: 9.7 crore. SIR 2026 (draft list): 7.78 crore. Which list was correct? For a government built on vote theft, the people are not important -- that's why this BJP neither listens to the people nor obeys their command," he said.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the BJP's “conspiracy to hollow out Indian democracy by stealing votes” is coming out into the open.&nbsp;“Where it suits the BJP, voters are added. Where it doesn't, votes are split to perpetrate 'vote theft'. Instead of acting as the guardian of fair elections, the EC is functioning like the 'Save BJP's Chair Commission'...The country is now uniting against vote theft. The nation has understood the BJP's conspiracy. The thief has been caught. Punishment will surely be meted out for holding democracy captive.”Congress Media and Publicity Department Chairman Pawan Khera said either the electoral rolls for the 2024 Maharashtra Assembly election were flawless, in which case the SIR has led to wrongful deletions or those rolls were questionable in which case Devendra Fadnavis is heading an "illegitimate" government."Only one of these two scenarios can be true. But either way, one conclusion is inescapable: The integrity of India’s elections has been compromised. And Gyanesh Gupta is the culprit," he said quoting Rahul's post. Khera has referred to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as Gyanesh Gupta.

stories.primary_headline: Four states move Supreme Court seeking quashing of 116 FIRs over NEET protests

primary_source.headline: Four states move Supreme Court seeking quashing of 116 FIRs over NEET protests
primary_source.content: New Delhi: States of Bihar, West Bengal, Maharashtra and Assam on Tuesday approached the Supreme Court seeking the quashing of 116 FIRs registered in connection with student protests held in July over the alleged NEET exam paper leak.They cited the central government’s commitment to the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) on July 25 that the cases would be withdrawn if the agitations were called off.The states urged the court to invoke its special powers under Article 142 of the Constitution.&nbsp;SC quashes FIRs on NEET protesters, allows fresh cases against 2,873 personsThe applications came a day after the Centre filed a similar plea to quash Delhi Police FIRs against protesters while seeking permission to register a single FIR against 2,873 persons with grave criminal antecedents.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta on Tuesday urged a bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant to list the states’ applications along with the Centre’s plea.&nbsp;The moves precede the CJP’s announcement of a fresh protest in Delhi on September 5, with the party contending that the Centre had not honoured its commitment.Bihar sought the quashing of 69 FIRs registered between July 20 and 27 across several districts, including cases at Gandhi Maidan and Kotwali in Patna, Gopalganj Town, Siwan Town, Jehanabad, Katihar Town, Muzaffarpur Town, Bihar Sharif, Bhagwan Bazar, Dumra, Punora, Lalganj and Bettiah.Maharashtra placed 34 FIRs before the court, covering cases in Nagpur, Mumbai, Pune, Jalgaon, Buldhana, Amravati and other locations. These included multiple FIRs from Shivaji Park and Sitabuldi police stations, as well as Ganesh Peth, Sadar, Azad Maidan, Chembur, Wadi, Deccan, Ambi and Ramtek. The state said that pursuant to the Centre’s July 25 decision, it no longer wished to pursue or investigate the listed cases.West Bengal also sought relief in respect of eight FIRs — one at Entally police station and seven at Hare Street police station. The state has undertaken not to oppose similar relief for any other related FIR that may come to its notice and has assured that no fresh FIR will be filed for the covered incidents.Assam listed five FIRs for quashing, stating that it no longer wished to pursue or investigate them following the central government’s July 25 decision.

stories.primary_headline: Supreme Court seeks Centre's view on introduction of totalisers for counting of votes in EVMs

primary_source.headline: Supreme Court seeks Centre's view on introduction of totalisers for counting of votes in EVMs
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Tuesday asked the Union government to state its position on introducing a “totaliser” system for counting votes recorded on Electronic Voting Machines, a mechanism that would aggregate results from multiple machines and prevent candidates from identifying voting patterns at individual polling booths.A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana specifically sought to know whether there were any impediments to the proposal and if it would have any adverse impact.&nbsp;West Bengal Assembly Elections 2026 | Strongrooms remain secure: EC dismisses TMC's EVM tampering claimThe Election Commission has also been directed to submit its proposal to the Union.The court was hearing three petitions that, among other reliefs, sought declaration of results at the constituency level rather than booth-wise. It asked whether a provision similar to Rule 59A of the Conduct of Elections Rules, 1961 — which permitted the use of a totaliser for ballot paper counting in certain circumstances — could be incorporated for EVMs, as recommended by the Law Commission in its 255th Report.&nbsp;The Union government was asked for its views since it held the power to amend the rules.A totaliser would allow votes from a cluster of EVMs to be counted together instead of booth by booth.Senior advocate Dama Seshadri Naidu, appearing for the EC, said the Commission had earlier approached the government on the issue. An expert committee and a Group of Ministers had examined the proposal but did not support it, and most political parties had also opposed the move. The EC had pointed out both the advantages and practical difficulties of the system.Advocate Ashwini Kumar Upadhyay, appearing in person as one of the petitioners, argued that the Commission’s present stand contradicted its earlier support for the totaliser. He submitted that aggregating votes from multiple EVMs would protect voter privacy and prevent post-poll victimisation and violence, as parties would not know which specific booths had voted against them.Chief Justice Surya Kant questioned the necessity of the change, noting that the existing booth-wise counting process was transparent and allowed scrutiny for discrepancies.&nbsp;“How does it benefit democracy,” he asked, pointing to the openness of the current system.Justice Bagchi, however, said that a totaliser was, in principle, a good tool for anonymising voter choice. But he pointed out the difficulty of the court issuing directions without statutory backing.&nbsp;He referred to Rule 59A and questioned why a similar provision could not be made applicable to EVMs.Senior advocate Gopal Sankaranarayanan, appearing in a connected matter, argued that the existing legal framework could be strengthened on the lines of the Law Commission’s recommendations and that courts had earlier nudged reforms such as NOTA and disclosure of candidates’ criminal antecedents.The EC, earlier in an affidavit, maintained that a totaliser ought not to be introduced at present, citing the absence of any enabling provision in the Constitution, the Representation of the People Acts or the Conduct of Election Rules. It said the move would dilute existing transparency safeguards, particularly the booth-wise correspondence between Parts I and II of Form 17C, which formed the backbone of the current self-verifying counting process.The Commission also flagged potential conflicts with Supreme Court directions on VVPAT verification and post-result checks of EVM microcontrollers, both of which presupposed the availability of distinct booth-wise and machine-wise results.

The unsigned opinion also cited the national security concerns that the government says the project would address. In the latest example of how Trump is using the FCC to harass reporters and news organizations that he dislikes, he said Meet the Press host Kristen Welker "will be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment" for what he claimed was a "purposeful inaccuracy."
"Kristen Welker, the Unpopular 'Hostess' of the once great Meet the Press, now considered Meet the Fake Press, just stated that Donald Trump has 'mixed results' on his Endorsements of Candidates, when the recent WINS of Darline Graham and Mike Mazzei, stand at 100% for the U.S. Senate, and 98% for the U.S. House, recently and over the longterm. How can anyone be allowed to say this, working for freely given Public Airwaves? Results are attached. Because of this purposeful inaccuracy, she will be reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment," Trump wrote in a Truth Social post.
A separate post from Trump yesterday said, "THE FAKE POLLS USED BY OUR CROOKED MEDIA ARE OUT OF CONTROL, AND SOMETHING MUST BE DONE ABOUT IT. FCC TO THE RESCUE! President DJT." Trump also posted a rant on Friday about New York Times journalist Maggie Haberman, calling her "an unattractive person both inside and out" who "should be forced to turn over any and all money that she’s made through her fake reporting on me." Trump referred to Haberman throughout his post as "Maggot Haberman."Read full article

primary_source.content: The president’s deportation machine is creating a class of people inside the US who have fewer protections against the power of the stateIs the Trump administration creating a group in the US with fewer protections against executive power owing to their immigration status? Its often openly racist actions suggest so. US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) claims to target “the worst of the worst” – undocumented migrants who commit violent crimes. Yet the Guardian reported that over half of those arrested in July had no criminal convictions or pending charges. That month, ICE made record arrests and deportations, apprehending 1,500 people and removing 1,100 daily.When campaigning, Donald Trump falsely claimed that Haitians were “eating the pets”. In office, his administration moved to end temporary protected status (TPS) for Haitians. In June, the supreme court let the protection expire, leaving about 350,000 people at risk of deportation to a country gripped by violence and instability. The court’s decision means more than 1 million TPS holders from 13 nations previously considered too unsafe to return to are now at risk of deportation. stories.primary_headline: Trump threatens to report journalist Kristen Welker to broadcast regulator

primary_source.headline: Trump threatens to report journalist Kristen Welker to broadcast regulator - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: United States President Donald Trump says he will report a prominent NBC television journalist to the federal agency in charge of regulating broadcast news outlets for “rebuke or punishment”. In a post on Truth Social on Sunday, Trump took issue with Kristen Welker’s characterisation of his endorsements of electoral candidates as having “mixed results” in the primaries leading up to November’s elections. “How can anyone be allowed to say this, working for freely given public airwaves?” Trump wrote. He also posted, without any attribution of where he got the data, a chart showing 98 percent of the candidates he endorsed had won their elections. “Because of this purposeful inaccuracy, she will be reported to the FCC,” the Federal Communications Commission, he said. Welker hosted the 2020 presidential election debate between Trump and former President Joe Biden and currently hosts NBC’s weekly news programme Meet the Press. In June, Welker had a one-on-one interview with Trump that ended in a heated exchange as she pressed the Republican president on continuing to claim the Democratic Party had cheated in the 2020 presidential election, in which Biden defeated Trump.

stories.primary_headline: Vote count under way in Iceland's knife-edge EU referendum

primary_source.headline: Vote count under way in Iceland’s knife-edge EU referendum - Al Jazeera
primary_source.content: Vote counting is under way in Iceland’s referendum on resuming membership negotiations with the European Union. Voting stations closed at 10pm local time on Saturday (22:00 GMT), and partial figures started emerging early on Sunday. Based on the initial 152,000 of an eligible 270,000 votes, 50.1 percent were against the government restarting talks with Brussels, according to broadcaster RUV, the Reuters news agency reported. That is a swing from an earlier Gallup poll, which gave the “yes” a slight lead. A final count is expected at about midday on Sunday, as counting up votes in the island country is a difficult challenge, with ballots coming from towns and rural polling stations by plane, boat, and car. The referendum does not have exit polls, and ballot counting only began once voting stations closed.
